$comment: The modules as data: the open package carries the base, handoff and decisionbook; per repository a person chooses which modules are on.
`base` is always wired; each module's `packages` in the order their hooks answer, and the rows in that order too (on /resume-handoff the handoff comes before
the decision book's shared part). `alias`: a short word a person may type for the module. `loses`: what a person reads when it is off.
`words`: the verbs those packages answer, so a verb typed while a package of the module is not installed says so instead of verb-unknown.
`optIn`: a module wired only when a person names it (setup --with <module>, setup --only, modules on); a plain setup leaves it off.
An add-on brings its own row: one of its packages holds it as `module` in its manifest (package.json `atlasbound`), in this shape. Such a
row is read only where that package is installed, is always `optIn`, and its packages answer before the rows here.

modules.name: handoff
modules.title: hand a session's work to the next one
modules.what: /handoff, atlasbound handoff, and the branch's note (your kept decisions and jobs first) at a session start and on /resume-handoff
modules.loses: you lose /handoff, atlasbound handoff and the branch's note at a session start and on /resume-handoff

modules.name: decisionbook
modules.title: why the code is so: decisions, plans, the plan gate
modules.what: /decisionbook, /decide, /resume-handoff's decisions, protect and the plan-before-code gate
modules.loses: you lose /decisionbook, /decide, the decisions on /resume-handoff and the plan gate before an edit
